raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
# Description

FP8BS grouped GEMM tests were being compared against a reference with FP32 accumulation. FP8BS on Blackwell via MXFP8 emulation passed these tests because MXFP8 grouped GEMM on Blackwell accumulates at a higher precision than native FP8BS grouped GEMM on Hopper.

This PR changes the reference in the test to the unfused split-grouped GEMM — consistent with how native MXFP8 grouped GEMM is tested.

## Type of change

- [ ] Documentation change (change only to the documentation, either a fix or a new content)
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Infra/Build change
- [ ] Code refactoring

# Checklist:

- [x] I have read and followed the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.rst)
- [x] The functionality is complete
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

Confidence Score: 5/5

**[Low impact]** The PR appears safe to merge, with a non-blocking request to retain the mixed-format rejection test.

Findings

1.  **Mixed formats lose test coverage** ▶

Summary

Replaces the FP32 reference with separately quantized, split GEMMs for the FP8 block-scaling and changing-splits CUDA graph tests. - FP8 grouped GEMM tests now use a quantized split reference. - FP8 grouped GEMM tests now cover empty and uneven expert groups. - The mixed-format operand rejection test is removed. Reviews (4) · Last reviewed commit: ["\[PyTorch\] Test grouped FP8 block-scaling..."](https://github.com/nvidia/transformerengine/commit/cc9d122d2572485b38941cd9cd156185f71dfe27) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_review&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=review_public&utm_content=nvidia/transformerengine)

**Scale differences are no longer stressed** Replacing the tile-scaled operands with plain `torch.randn` removes deliberate differences between FP8 block scales. This matters especially for `weight_block_dim=2`, where large blocks of normally distributed values have similar maxima. A bug that reads another block's scale could then be harder to catch. Keep the per-tile power-of-two factors while using the new split-GEMM reference. The reference no longer needs exactly representable operands. Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time!

The replacement cases use matching formats, so a later change could stop rejecting mixed formats on Blackwell without failing these tests. Keep the negative test and switch its inputs to `_tile_scaled_randn`; it does not depend on the old FP32 reference. Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time!

inline_comments.body: **Scale differences are no longer stressed** Replacing the tile-scaled operands with plain `torch.randn` removes deliberate differences between FP8 block scales. This matters especially for `weight_block_dim=2`, where large blocks of normally distributed values have similar maxima. A bug that reads another block's scale could then be harder to catch. Keep the per-tile power-of-two factors while using the new split-GEMM reference. The reference no longer needs exactly representable operands. Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time!

Confidence Score: 5/5

**[Low impact]** The PR appears safe to merge, with a non-blocking request to retain the mixed-format rejection test.

Findings

1.  **Mixed formats lose test coverage** ▶

Summary

Replaces the FP32 reference with separately quantized, split GEMMs for the FP8 block-scaling and changing-splits CUDA graph tests. - FP8 grouped GEMM tests now use a quantized split reference. - FP8 grouped GEMM tests now cover empty and uneven expert groups. - The mixed-format operand rejection test is removed.
